So first, yes, many police attack teams wear hard body armor plates in addition to the soft armor. Armor has different ratings based on what it attempts to stop.

When we look at rifle plates, like Level III armor, we usually see they're made of either hard metal like AR500 or ceramic composite plates.

AR500 is cheaper and more durable, but heavier and can deflect spalling damage into your throat.

Ceramics are more expensive and completely crumble after several rounds, but are lighter and capture spall.

Let's look at some plate tests by various people with various weapons and rounds at various ranges to see which may be better:

5.56x45 XM193 from a 22" barrel at 7 yards

7.62x39 122gr Tulammo from a 16" barrel at 45 feet

7.62x51 and 5.56x45 M855 green tip vs three different plates

I suggest anyone considering body armor watch all three of those videos before committing.

I also suggest equally strongly that anyone interested in home defense ammo watch them. Pistols and shotguns can never reliably get through plate and kevlar. The answer is careful rifle and ammunition selection.
